paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of knowledge probing on BioMedLM after applying six different editing methods, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 0 to approximately 10⁴ and the y-axis showing accuracy from 35% to 65%. The “Base” model (black line with circular markers, solid line) starts at approximately 38% accuracy at low co-occurrence and plateaus near 44% across higher values. “FT” (blue line with downward-triangle markers, solid line) begins around 40% and rises steadily to about 48%. “IKE” (red line with upward-triangle markers, solid line) starts near 43%, increases more steeply than FT, and reaches approximately 50% at the highest co-occurrence. “MEND” (brown line with diamond markers, solid line) begins at ~44%, rises to ~56% at 10⁴. “MEMIT” (purple line with pentagon markers, solid line) starts at ~44%, climbs to ~55% at 10⁴. “ROME” (green line with square markers, solid line) starts at ~51% and consistently leads all methods, reaching approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All methods show a positive correlation between co-occurrence frequency and accuracy, with ROME maintaining the highest performance throughout.
